safe_consumption: Safe for consumption within recommended limits. Avoid excessive intake due to potential toxicity when exposed to acidic conditions or ingested beyond the daily dietary allowance.

name: Potassium ferrocyanide
description: A synthetic product used as an anti-caking agent and to remove copper from red wine.
safe_consumption: Safe below daily intake levels; avoid consumption if exposed to high acidity environments or ingesting large quantities regularly due to potential toxicity under certain conditions.

name: Ferrous hexacyanomanganate
description: Potassium ferrocyanide is a synthetic product used as an anticaking agent.
health_concerns: unstable and toxic in acid solutions
safe_consumption: Safe for consumption below the daily intake. Avoid acidic foods to prevent instability.

name: Calcium ferrocyanide
description: A synthetic product used as a stabilizer and anticaking agent in food.
health_concerns: unstable and toxic in acid solutions
safe_consumption: Calcium ferrocyanide is safe for consumption at doses below the daily intake. However, it becomes unstable and potentially harmful when exposed to acidic conditions.

name: Sodium thiosulfate
description: A synthetic additive used as an antioxidant and sequestrant, produced mainly from industrial waste.

name: Dicalcium diphosphate
description: Synthetic additive, obtained from phosphoric acid derivative.

name: Sodium aluminium phosphates
description: A synthetic additive used as an emulsifier in processed cheese and a stabilizer in baking powder.
health_concerns: possible neurotoxic effects linked to Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases
safe_consumption: Consume within recommended limits. Avoid excessive intake due to potential health risks associated with high levels of consumption.

name: Bone phosphate
description: A food additive derived from animal bones, consisting of tricalcium phosphate.
health_concerns: possible link with bovine spongiform encephalopathy
safe_consumption: Avoid if possible due to health concerns. Consult a healthcare provider for personalized advice.

name: Calcium sodium polyphosphate
description: A food additive used as an emulsifier to improve texture and stability in processed foods.
safe_consumption: Generally recognized as safe for consumption within the approved limits set by regulatory authorities. Always check labels before consuming products containing this additive.

name: Calcium Polyphosphates
description: A calcium salt derived from phosphoric acid, used as an emulsifier and stabilizer in food products.
safe_consumption: In large doses can cause hyperactivity and digestive issues. Consume within recommended limits to avoid adverse effects.
common_foods: processed foods containing phosphoric acid derivatives

name: Ammonium Polyphosphates
description: A chemical compound used as a stabilizer and regulator in food products.
health_concerns: Potential health risks linked to consumption
safe_consumption: Consume within recommended limits. Excessive intake may pose moderate concerns for some individuals.

name: Magnesium pyrophosphate
description: A natural salt formed by heating phosphates, used as a stabilizer and regulator in food.
safe_consumption: May cause loss of bone calcium. In children can lead to hyperactivity or behavioral issues according to some studies; consult a healthcare provider if concerned.

name: Sodium silicates
description: A chemical compound used as an anticaking and stabilizing additive in various food products.
safe_consumption: Avoid direct contact with the product. Do not ingest unless specifically directed by a healthcare provider or as part of prescribed medication containing sodium silicate.

name: Silicon dioxide

source: Synthetic, Plant-derived (Silica naturally found in plant foods)

name: Calcium silicate
description: A calcium compound used as an anticaking and stabilizing additive in various food products.

name: Magnesium silicates
description: A natural crystalline mineral used as an anticaking and thickening additive in food products.

name: (i) Magnesium silicate (ii) Magnesium trisilicate
description: A synthetic additive used to prevent clumping in powdered foods.
safe_consumption: Generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by food safety authorities. Used within specified limits for anti-caking purposes.

name: Talc
description: A mineral used as an anti-caking additive in various foods.
safe_consumption: Generally considered safe for consumption within the approved limits set by food safety authorities. Avoid excessive intake if concerned about potential health impacts.

name: Sodium aluminosilicate
description: A synthetic additive used as an anticaking and stabilizing ingredient in various foods.

common_foods: processed foods containing salt or other additives

name: Potassium aluminium silicate
description: A potassium salt of silicic aluminum used as an anticaking additive.
health_concerns: linked to Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's
safe_consumption: Avoid consumption if possible. Consult a healthcare provider for advice.

name: Aluminium Calcium Silicate
description: Calcium silicoaluminate, an industrially produced mineral species of the group of silicates (anortite), used as a food additive.

name: Zinc silicate
description: A mineral additive used to prevent food particles from sticking.

name: Bentonite

safe_consumption: Bentonite is generally considered safe for consumption. No side effects have been found in studies.

name: Aluminium silicate
description: A white clay composed mainly of aluminum silicates, used as an anticaking and exfoliating additive in food products.
health_concerns: Contains aluminium which may pose health risks

name: Potassium silicate
description: A potassium salt of silicic acid, produced by supercooled fusion of potassium carbonate and pure silica sand.
health_concerns: Not much is known about the toxicity
safe_consumption: Limited studies on long-term consumption effects. Use as directed in food products.

name: Vermiculite
description: A mineral used as a soil amendment and absorbent.
safe_consumption: Generally safe for consumption in food products. Used primarily outside of direct human ingestion, such as agricultural applications or industrial uses where it may come into contact with foods indirectly through the environment.

name: Sepiolite
description: A mineral used as a food additive.
safe_consumption: Safe for consumption in small amounts. More research needed on long-term effects.

name: Sepiolitic clay
description: A type of mineral additive derived from the sedimentary deposits containing organic matter.
safe_consumption: Generally safe for consumption in small quantities as per FSSAI guidelines. Avoid excessive intake due to potential health concerns identified by some studies.

name: Lignosulfonates
description: A food additive derived from lignin, a component of wood and bark.
safe_consumption: Generally recognized as safe for consumption in small quantities. Avoid excessive intake if possible.

name: Natrolite-phonolite
description: A food additive derived from magnesium carbonates, used as a carrier in various foods.
safe_consumption: Generally safe for consumption. Follow recommended dietary guidelines and consult with healthcare providers if you have specific health concerns or allergies.

name: Fatty acids
description: A group of molecules derived from animal and plant fats used as emulsifiers in food products.
safe_consumption: Avoid in large doses due to potential health concerns.

name: Ammonium stearate
description: A salt of stearic acid used as an anti-caking and anti-foaming additive in sugar production.
source: Mineral-derived (from plant sources, but animal fat origin cannot be excluded)
safe_consumption: Avoid direct contact with powder. Do not inhale the dust when handling in powdered form.

name: Magnesium stearate
description: A chemical compound used as an anticaking and flow aid in food products.
safe_consumption: Generally safe for consumption. Avoid inhaling the powder during handling to prevent potential health risks.

name: Aluminium stearate
description: A salt synthesized from stearic acid and aluminum, used as an anticaking agent.
safe_consumption: At recommended doses no side effects have been found. But large doses can lead to toxicity and accumulation concerns.

name: Gluconic acid
description: A naturally occurring organic compound derived from glucose, used as a stabilizer and regulator in food products.
safe_consumption: Gluconic acid is generally recognized as safe for consumption. It should be consumed within the recommended dietary guidelines established by health authorities.

name: Glucono delta-lactone
description: A food additive used as a sequestrant, acidifier or curing agent.
safe_consumption: Generally considered safe for consumption in accordance with regulatory standards. No known side effects have been found.

name: Sodium gluconate
description: A food additive derived from glucose, used as a stabilizer and regulator of acidity in various foods.
safe_consumption: Sodium gluconate is generally recognized as safe for consumption by the general population. No significant health concerns have been identified at typical levels found in food products.

name: Potassium Gluconate
description: A potassium salt derived from gluconic acid, used as a stabilizer and regulator in many products.
safe_consumption: Potassium Gluconate is generally recognized as safe for consumption. No known side effects have been found with its use within the approved limits set by food safety authorities globally.

name: Calcium Gluconate
description: A mineral supplement and medication derived from calcium gluconate.
safe_consumption: Calcium Gluconate is generally considered safe for consumption. No side effects have been found in commercial use, but as with any additive, it should be consumed according to recommended dietary guidelines and within the context of a balanced diet.

name: Ferrous gluconate
description: Iron salt of gluconic acid used as a colour and iron supplement.
safe_consumption: Generally safe for consumption. No known side effects have been found in studies.

name: Magnesium gluconate
description: A mineral supplement used to provide magnesium in the diet.
safe_consumption: Generally safe for consumption as per EFSA guidelines. Follow recommended dietary allowances (RDAs).

name: Ferrous lactate
description: Iron salt derived from lactic acid, used as a stabilizer and regulator in food products.
health_concerns: May pose minor health risks for some individuals
safe_consumption: Consume within recommended dietary allowances. Excessive consumption may lead to adverse effects.
common_foods: Various processed foods containing iron supplements or fortifications

name: Hexylresorcinol
description: A chemical compound used as an antioxidant in food products.
safe_consumption: Avoid ingestion; can cause allergic or intolerance reactions. Harmful if ingested, causing skin, eye, and respiratory irritations.

name: Synthetic calcium aluminates
description: A synthetic additive used in food processing, primarily as a stabilizer and thickener.
safe_consumption: Generally safe for consumption within recommended limits. Avoid excessive intake of calcium-rich foods containing this additive to prevent potential health issues related to high dietary calcium levels.

name: Perlite
description: A mineral used as a soil amendment and sometimes in food processing.
safe_consumption: Perlite is generally recognized as safe for consumption. However, it should not be ingested intentionally due to its abrasive nature which can cause harm if swallowed or inhaled during handling.

name: Glutamic acid
description: A natural amino acid used as a flavour enhancer.
health_concerns: Potential excitotoxicity and neurotoxicity in high doses
Can cause allergic reactions and asthma attacks
safe_consumption: Consume within recommended limits to avoid health risks

name: Monosodium L-glutamate
description: Sodium salt of glutamic acid, a naturally occurring amino acid that enhances flavor.

name: Monopotassium L-glutamate

name: Calcium di-L-glutamate
description: A calcium salt derived from glutamic acid, a natural amino acid that is an excitatory neurotransmitter in the central nervous system.
safe_consumption: Consume as part of your regular diet, but be aware it may cause adverse reactions if consumed excessively due to its potential for causing neurological damage.

name: Monoammonium L-glutamate
description: A flavour enhancing additive derived from glutamic acid, linked to excitotoxicity and neurotoxicity in high doses.

name: Magnesium di-L-glutamate
description: A flavour enhancing additive derived from magnesium salts of glutamic acid.
health_concerns: potentially excitotoxic and neurotoxic in high doses
safe_consumption: Consume as per recommended dietary guidelines. Avoid excessive intake to prevent potential health risks.

name: Guanylic acid
description: A natural compound derived from RNA, used as a flavouring agent.

description: A natural salt of the nucleotide guanosine monophosphate (GMP), enhancing flavor and reducing required sodium in foods.

Guanylates may not be used in products intended for children under 12 weeks

description: A flavour enhancing salt derived from inosinic acid, chemically bound with potassium.
source: Animal-derived (from Torula yeast or meat/fish fermentation)

description: A flavour enhancing additive derived from inosinic acid, chemically bound with potassium.

name: Maltol
description: A synthetic flavouring agent derived from larch bark, pine needles and other sources.

name: Ethyl Maltol
description: A flavour enhancing additive derived from ethylenically maltol, significantly sweeter than its precursor.
safe_consumption: Safe in small quantities; avoid large doses due to potential health risks. Not recommended for consumption by pregnant women or individuals with known sensitivities.

name: Alanine

name: Glycine and its sodium salt

safe_consumption: Safe for consumption within recommended limits. Avoid excessive intake as it may cause allergic reactions or other health issues in sensitive individuals.

name: Lysin hydrochloride
description: A synthetic amino acid used as a flavouring agent.

name: Zinc acetate

name: Oleandomycin

name: Penicillin G sodium

name: Penicillin G procaine

name: Penicillin G benzathine
description: A synthetic antibiotic used for treating bacterial infections.

name: Spiramycins

name: Virginiamycins

name: Tylosin

name: Avoparcin

name: Salinomycin

name: Polydimethylsiloxane

name: Methylphenylpolysiloxane

name: Carnauba wax

name: Shellac

name: Paraffins

name: Lanolin

name: Oxidized polyethylene wax

description: A chemical used to improve dough strength and volume in baking.
safe_consumption: Avoid consumption if possible due to potential health risks. Follow food labels for presence of Potassium bromate.
common_foods: bread and baked goods containing flour or wheat products

name: Potassium bromate
description: Synthetic compound used in flour to strengthen dough, produced by reacting potassium hydroxide with bromine.
safe_consumption: Avoid consumption due to toxicity and potential carcinogenicity. Not advisable for ingestion or contact.

name: Calcium bromate
description: A synthetic compound used in flour and cosmetics, toxic by ingestion or contact.
safe_consumption: Avoid consumption. Not safe for human use due to toxicity concerns.

name: Chlorine
description: A gas with a stifling odor that is extremely toxic and used as a flour treatment (bleaching) agent.
safe_consumption: Not recommended due to high toxicity concerns. Avoid consumption if possible, especially in its gaseous form or from contaminated sources like water treated with chlorine disinfectants.

name: Chlorine dioxide
description: A synthetic gas used as a bleaching and disinfecting agent in flour production.
safe_consumption: Not recommended for consumption due to high toxicity risks. Avoid inhalation or contact with skin, eyes and mucous membranes.

name: Azodicarbonamide
description: Used to strengthen flour and improve its elasticity.
safe_consumption: Avoid consumption if allergic or sensitive. Follow label instructions for safe use in cooking.

name: Urea (Carbamide)
description: A chemical compound used as a flour treatment agent, obtained from ammonia and carbon dioxide.
safe_consumption: Avoid ingestion due to acute health risks. Safe for use in food products as per JECFA guidelines.

name: Benzoyl peroxide
description: A chemical used for whitening and as a preservative in various products.
safe_consumption: Not recommended due to high health risks associated with consumption. Avoid contact or inhalation of dust during handling.

name: Acetone peroxide
description: A primary explosive discovered in 1895, acetone peroxide is an unstable and hazardous chemical compound.
safe_consumption: Not for consumption. Highly dangerous if ingested due to its instability and potential explosiveness.

name: Calcium peroxide
description: A chemical compound used as a flour enhancer and bleach, which can release hydrogen peroxide upon contact with acids.
safe_consumption: Not recommended for consumption due to its corrosive nature and potential health hazards if ingested or inhaled. Avoid direct skin, eye, respiratory tract contact with calcium peroxide.

name: Argon
description: Natural inert gas used as a propellant in canned products.
safe_consumption: Argon is generally recognized as safe for consumption and use within the context of its application. No direct ingestion occurs, but it may be present indirectly through packaged foods containing Argon gas under pressure.

name: Helium
description: A natural inert gas used as a propellant and stabilizer for packaged products, including those sensitive to air or oxygen.
safe_consumption: Helium is non-toxic under standard conditions. No side effects have been found in large-scale use through fractional distillation of natural gas.

name: Dichlorodifluormethane
description: A propellant used in aerosols, banned since 1995 due to ozone depletion and greenhouse gas effects.
safe_consumption: Not recommended for consumption as it is toxic when inhaled from aerosol sprays. Avoid ingestion or contact with skin, eyes, nose, throat, and lungs.

name: Nitrogen
description: A chemical element used as a propellant and stabilizer in packaged products, including beers for carbonation.
safe_consumption: Nitrogen is generally recognized as safe when consumed within the context of its intended use. No known health risks associated with consumption at levels found naturally or added to foods and beverages in accordance with regulatory standards.

name: Nitrous oxide
description: A chemical compound, an oxide of nitrogen with the formula N2O.
health_concerns: classified as a pollutant by Kyoto Protocol
toxic if used in high doses
safe_consumption: Safe when not consumed directly or inhaled. Not recommended during pregnancy, especially first trimester.

name: Butane
description: Used as a propellant in food processing and packaging, butane is also found in cigarette lighters.
safe_consumption: Avoid inhalation or ingestion; not intended for consumption as a dietary additive due to health risks.

name: Isobutane
description: A hydrocarbon gas used as a propellant in food products.
safe_consumption: Not intended to be consumed directly; may pose health risks if inhaled or ingested accidentally. Always use with caution and follow safety guidelines when handling.

name: Propane
description: A gas derived from petroleum products used as a chemical energy source by combustion in engines, barbecues and boilers. Commonly utilized for fuel, solvent, coolant, food additive purposes including vegetable oils spray.
safe_consumption: Propane is generally safe when handled properly but can pose risks if inhaled or ingested in large quantities due to its flammability and potential asphyxiation hazard. Always use with caution, especially around open flames.

name: Chloropentafluorethane
description: A chlorofluorocarbon (CFC) used as a refrigerant, known for its potential to destroy ozone.
safe_consumption: Not safe due to health risks and banned in many countries. Avoid inhalation of vapors, contact with gas/liquefied form.

name: Octafluorcyclobutane
description: A transparent, colorless gas with an ethereal odor used as a propellant.
safe_consumption: Not for consumption. Can cause dizziness, suffocation and respiratory issues upon inhalation or contact.

name: Oxygen
description: A propellant used in aerosols and packaging.
safe_consumption: Not determined. Avoid inhalation of concentrated oxygen gas due to potential health risks such as respiratory issues or hypoxia when exposed directly from aerosol cans without proper ventilation.

name: Hydrogen
description: A colorless and odorless natural gas used in packaging.
safe_consumption: Hydrogen is safe for consumption as it occurs naturally. However, its use should be limited to the intended purpose of being a food additive or preservative due to potential health risks associated with inhalation in large quantities.

name: Acesulfame potassium
description: An artificial sweetener approximately 200 times sweeter than sugar, stable to heat.
safe_consumption: Consuming in moderation as per food labels. Avoid excessive intake due to health concerns identified by EFSA.

name: Aspartame
description: Artificial sweetener used as a sugar substitute in some foods and beverages.
health_concerns: formation of different forms of cancer
safe_consumption: Aspartame is generally recognized as safe for consumption by regulatory agencies, but individuals may experience varying responses to its intake. It should be consumed in moderation.

name: Cyclamates
description: A synthetic low calorie sweetener, Cyclamic acid and its salts are up to 40 times sweeter than sugar but less sweet.
safe_consumption: Avoid consumption due to potential health risks. Not recommended for regular use in diets, especially not by pregnant women or children under the age of two.

name: Isomalt
description: A sugar substitute with minimal impact on blood glucose levels.
health_concerns: No side effects have been found in large doses
safe_consumption: Isomalt is widely used for the production of sugar-free candy and other products. No significant health concerns reported at recommended consumption levels.

name: Saccharins
description: An artificial sweetening additive derived from toluene and anthranilic acid, linked with cancer in laboratory animals.
safe_consumption: Consume only as directed on the label. Avoid excessive consumption due to potential health risks identified in studies.

name: Sucralose
description: Synthetic low calorie sweetener, up to 600 times sweeter than sugar.
health_concerns: destruction of the immune system affecting mainly the liver and kidneys
safe_consumption: Consumption should be limited as it can cause health issues in large doses. More research is needed to fully understand its long-term effects.

name: Alitame
description: Synthetic low calorie sweetener, up to 2000 times sweeter than sugar.
safe_consumption: No side effects have been found at the moment. But it is an additive that does not have much information about its toxicity in humans.

name: Thaumatin
description: A sugar protein, traditionally derived from the African tropical plant 'katemfe', used to modify flavors and not exclusively as a sweetener.
safe_consumption: Thaumatin is generally safe for consumption, but high doses may cause digestive issues. It should be consumed in moderation according to the recommended guidelines.

name: Glycyrrhizin
description: A natural sweetener derived from licorice root, with aniseed and bittersweet flavor.
safe_consumption: Use in moderation due to potential health concerns at high doses. Suitable for diabetics as a sugar substitute, but monitor intake closely if you have conditions like hypertension or low potassium levels.

name: Neohesperidine dihydrochalcone
description: An artificial sweetener derived from grapefruit seed, sweeter than sugar and used to mask bitter flavors.
health_concerns: can cause migraines in large doses
safe_consumption: Generally safe for consumption but may not be suitable as a primary ingredient due to potential health concerns at high intake levels. Use sparingly and according to manufacturer recommendations.

name: Steviol glycosides
description: A natural sweetener extracted from the Stevia plant, significantly sweeter than sucrose.
health_concerns: linked to health risks in studies
safe_consumption: Consuming within established ADI limits is considered safe for most individuals. However, some may experience adverse reactions or concerns regarding its safety.

name: Neotame
description: Synthetic low calorie sweetener and flavor enhancer.
safe_consumption: Considered toxic, better avoid it. Up to 13,000 times sweeter than sugar; may pose significant risks similar or worse compared to aspartame.

name: Aspartame-acesulfame
description: An artificial sweetener marketed under the name Twinsweet, manufactured by mixing aspartame E951 and acesulfame E950.
health_concerns: linked to health risks in studies
safe_consumption: May cause minor allergic reactions or gastrointestinal issues for some individuals. Avoid if you have sensitivities to artificial sweeteners.

name: Tagatose
description: A sweetening agent derived from lactose, typically obtained industrially.
source: Plant-derived (from dairy products and some fruits)
safe_consumption: Safe for consumption in moderate amounts. Do not consume excessively as it may cause gastrointestinal discomfort such as diarrhea or nausea.

name: Polyglycitol syrup
description: A sweetening agent derived from hydrogenated starch hydrolyzates, containing maltitol and sorbitol.
safe_consumption: May cause mild laxative effects or gastric discomfort in sensitive individuals. Generally safe for consumption within recommended limits.

name: Maltitols
description: A sugar alcohol used as a sweet substitute with properties similar to sucrose, but without causing browning.
safe_consumption: Consume in moderation. May not be suitable for individuals sensitive to sugar alcohols or those following a low FODMAP diet due to potential gastrointestinal discomfort.

name: Lactitol
description: A sugar alcohol derived from lactose, used as a sweetener.
safe_consumption: In small doses can cause laxative effects; avoid in children under 3 years. Combined with other sweeteners for desired sweetness.

name: Xylitol
description: A natural carbohydrate alcohol used as a sugar substitute in various products.
safe_consumption: Consume within recommended limits to avoid digestive issues. Avoid excessive intake of more than the daily limit suggested by health authorities.

name: Erythritol
description: A sugar alcohol that is considered safe as a food additive, almost noncaloric and does not affect blood sugar or cause tooth decay.
safe_consumption: Safe for consumption within recommended limits. Avoid excessive intake to prevent laxative effects.

name: Advantame
description: Synthetic low calorie sweetener derived from Aspartame and Vanillin, up to 37,000 times sweeter than sugar.
safe_consumption: Consume in moderation as per recommended dietary guidelines. Avoid excessive intake due to potential health concerns like laxative effects and diarrhea.

name: Quillaia extracts
description: A South American tree extract used in supplements and slimming pills to satisfy hunger.
safe_consumption: May pose moderate health risks; consult a healthcare provider before use. Avoid if allergic or sensitive to tree extracts.

name: Cholic acid
description: A bile component synthesized from cholesterol, used as an emulsifier in food products.
safe_consumption: Generally considered safe for consumption. No known side effects reported to date.
common_foods: Various processed foods containing animal derivatives

name: Choline salts and esters
description: A chemical compound used as an emulsifying agent to mix substances like oil and water.
safe_consumption: Generally considered safe for consumption in small amounts. No known secondary effects reported.

name: Amylases
description: A digestive enzyme that breaks down starches into sugars.
safe_consumption: May cause allergic reactions in sensitive individuals. Moderation is advised for those with allergies or sensitivities to animal products.

name: Proteases
description: Enzymes that catalyze the hydrolysis of peptide bonds in proteins.
source: Plant-derived, Animal-derived (from sources like papain and bromelain)
safe_consumption: Generally safe for consumption. Used as a food additive to soften meat or tenderize fish fillets.

name: Glucose oxidase
description: A natural enzyme that helps break down sugar into its metabolites.
source: Microorganisms (fungi) Aspergillus niger or penicillium notatum
safe_consumption: Generally considered safe for consumption in small amounts as per FSSAI guidelines. Avoid excessive intake if allergic reactions occur.

name: Invertases
description: An enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of sucrose into fructose and glucose, used in food production like honey.
safe_consumption: Generally considered safe for consumption. No known side effects have been found.

name: Lipases
description: Enzymes that catalyze the hydrolysis of fats into glycerol and fatty acids, used as a flavouring agent.
safe_consumption: Generally considered safe for consumption in small quantities. May cause allergic reactions or digestive issues in sensitive individuals.

name: Lysozyme
description: An antimicrobial enzyme that forms part of the innate immune system in animals.
safe_consumption: May cause allergic reactions to individuals with egg allergies. Generally considered safe for most people, but caution is advised if you have an existing shellfish or fish allergy due to potential cross-reactivity concerns.

name: Polydextroses
description: A polymer of glucose and sorbitol, used as a thickening agent in sugar-free products.
safe_consumption: Generally safe for consumption. May cause mild digestive issues like flatulence or diarrhea at high doses.

name: Polyvinylpyrrolidone
description: Synthetic polymer used as a thickening, filling agent and stabilizer in pharmaceuticals.
safe_consumption: Consume with caution due to potential health risks identified in laboratory studies. Avoid high doses.

name: Polyvinylpolypyrrolidone
description: Synthetic polymer used as a stabilizer in beverages, pharmaceuticals and cosmetics.
safe_consumption: Avoid large doses. Not mandatory to indicate its use on labels due to potential long-term presence in the body despite known risks.

name: Polyvinyl alcohol
description: A synthetic polymer obtained by alkaline hydrolysis of polyvinyl acetate, used as a thickening agent in food.
health_concerns: presence of toxic residues like methanol and methyl acetate
safe_consumption: Limited data available; potential health risks due to residual toxins. Use recommended by manufacturers only if necessary, as a last resort for individuals with specific dietary needs.

name: Pullulan
description: A polysaccharide derived from starch fermented by the fungus Aureobasidium pullulans, used as a thickening agent in various food products.
safe_consumption: Generally considered safe for consumption. No known side effects reported.

name: Basic methacrylate copolymer
description: A food additive used as a coating for solid foods and supplements, derived from methacrylic acid polymerization.
safe_consumption: Limited consumption guidance due to insufficient toxicity information. Use within specified limits recommended by EFSA.

name: Vinyl Acetate Copolymer
description: A synthetic polymer used as a coating and disintegrant in various products.
safe_consumption: Avoid consumption of large doses. Not mandatory to indicate its use on labels, but it is believed not safe for long-term ingestion due to potential health risks identified in animal studies.

name: Polyvinyl alcohol graft copolymer
description: A synthetic material used as a protective film in solid food products.
safe_consumption: Generally safe for consumption, but limited studies on long-term effects exist. Used primarily with caution and recommended to avoid overconsumption of coated foods.

name: Dextrins, roasted starch
description: A group of low-molecular-weight carbohydrates produced by the hydrolysis of starch or glycogen, used as a thickening agent in various foods.
safe_consumption: Generally safe for consumption. May cause minor digestive issues in sensitive individuals due to its high carbohydrate content.

name: Acid-treated starch
description: A thickening agent derived from tapioca, rice or potato starches that have been chemically modified with acid.
source: Plant-derived (from natural sources like tapioca, rice, potatoes)
health_concerns: transgenic raw materials may pose health risks
safe_consumption: Consume in moderation as part of a balanced diet. Avoid excessive intake due to potential chemical modification concerns.

name: Alkaline treated starch
description: Prepared by treating starch or starch granules with sodium-or potassium hydroxide. The starch is partially degraded.
safe_consumption: Acceptable Daily Intake not determined; in large doses can cause hyperactivity and digestive discomfort.

name: Bleached starch
description: A thickening agent derived from corn, potatoes or wheat that has been bleached and possibly oxidized.
safe_consumption: May cause allergic reactions in sensitive individuals. Moderately safe for consumption but should be used sparingly due to potential health concerns linked with bleaching agents like sodium hypochlorite.

name: Oxidized starch
description: A thickening agent derived from oxidised corn, potatoes or wheat used in various food products.
health_concerns: Potentially toxic compounds formed during oxidation
May contain transgenic materials if not labeled
safe_consumption: Moderate consumption is generally considered safe. Individuals with sensitivities should monitor intake closely.

name: Starches, enzyme treated
description: A food additive derived from corn or potatoes that has been processed with enzymes to break down its starches, commonly used as a thickening agent in various foods.
safe_consumption: Generally safe for consumption. Individuals sensitive or allergic should avoid it and consult with healthcare providers if necessary.

name: Monostarch phosphate
description: A food additive used as a thickening agent, derived from corn starch and phosphoric acid.
health_concerns: May contain genetically modified organisms if not specified
safe_consumption: Generally safe when consumed in moderation. Check labels to avoid products with transgenic ingredients or high levels of phosphates.

name: Distarch glycerol
description: A thickening agent derived from modified starches made using corn, potatoes or wheat.
safe_consumption: Generally safe for consumption in small quantities. Avoid excessive intake due to potential allergens and transgenic origins.

name: Distarch phosphate
description: A thickening agent derived from modified starches, often used in sauces and dairy products.
safe_consumption: Generally safe for consumption. May cause mild allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

name: Phosphated distarch phosphate
description: A thickening agent derived from modified starches, used in various food products.
safe_consumption: Generally safe for consumption. Individuals with specific allergies or sensitivities should consult a healthcare provider before use.

name: Acetylated distarch phosphate
description: A chemical modification of starch used as a thickening agent in various foods.
safe_consumption: Generally safe for consumption. May pose minor concerns to individuals with specific allergies or sensitivities.

name: Starch acetate
description: A chemically modified starch used as a thickening agent in various food products.
safe_consumption: Generally safe for consumption. May pose minor concerns to individuals with specific allergies or sensitivities.

name: Starch acetate esterified with vinyl acetate
description: A chemical modification of starch using treatment with vinyl acetate, used as a thickening agent in various food products.
health_concerns: Chemical modifications may pose health risks
safe_consumption: Generally safe for consumption. Individuals sensitive to chemicals should monitor intake closely.

name: Acetylated distarch adipate
description: A thickening agent derived from modified starches, used in various sauces and dairy products.
safe_consumption: Generally safe for consumption. Individuals with specific allergies should consult a healthcare provider before use.

name: Acetylated distarch glycerol
description: A thickening additive used in various food products.
safe_consumption: Generally considered safe for consumption within the approved limits set by regulatory bodies. Always check labels and recommended daily intake on packaging to ensure safety.

name: Distarch glycerine (stabiliser)
description: A thickening additive derived from starch and glycerol, commonly used in food products to improve texture.
safe_consumption: Distarch glycerine is generally recognized as safe for consumption within the approved limits set by regulatory authorities. It should not be consumed excessively due to potential digestive issues at high intakes.

name: Hydroxypropyl starch
description: A thickening agent derived from corn, potatoes or wheat modified with propylene oxide.
health_concerns: Concerns related to genetically modified organisms
safe_consumption: Generally safe for consumption in small quantities as per EU regulations. Individuals sensitive should consult a healthcare provider before use.
common_foods: Cooking cream, yoghurts, puddings, custards, desserts

name: Hydoxypropyl di-starch glycerol
description: A chemical modification of starches derived from corn, potatoes or wheat using propylene oxide and epichlorohydrin.
health_concerns: May cause digestive issues in sensitive individuals
safe_consumption: Generally safe for consumption. May not be suitable for those with specific allergies or sensitivities to starches and related compounds.

name: Hydroxypropyl distarch phosphate
description: A food additive used as a thickening agent, derived from corn starch.
safe_consumption: Generally safe for consumption in small quantities. Individuals with allergies or sensitivities should consult healthcare providers before use.

name: Hydroxy propyl distarch glycerol
description: A food additive used as an emulsifier, stabilizer and thickener.
safe_consumption: Generally considered safe for consumption in accordance with current regulations. Always check labels before consuming products containing this ingredient.

name: Starch sodium octenyl succinate
description: A chemical modification of starch used as a thickening agent in various food products.
safe_consumption: Generally safe for consumption. Check labels if you have specific dietary restrictions.

name: Acetylated oxidised starch
description: A thickening agent derived from corn, potatoes or wheat treated with sodium hypochlorite and anhydrous acetic acid.
safe_consumption: Generally safe for consumption in moderation. Check labels if you have specific dietary restrictions.

name: Starch aluminium octenyl succinate
description: A chemical additive used as a thickening agent in various food products.
safe_consumption: Consuming this ingredient within recommended limits is generally considered safe for most people. However, individuals with specific allergies or sensitivities should consult a healthcare provider.

name: Benzylated hydrocarbons
description: Natural compounds used in flavor and fragrance, produced chemically.
safe_consumption: Generally considered safe for consumption. No known effect when consumed as food additives at approved levels.

name: Butane-1,3-diol
description: A chemical additive used as a solvent for flavors and in tobacco products.
health_concerns: Limited knowledge about its effects on human body
safe_consumption: Consumption should be limited due to moderate health concerns identified by studies. Further research is needed.

name: Castor oil
description: Natural anticaking and flavoring additive derived from Ricinus communis seeds.
safe_consumption: Castor oil should be consumed in moderation. Avoid excessive intake to prevent diarrhea or severe dehydration.

name: Ethyl acetate
description: A natural component of many fruits, commercially produced from acetic acid. Used as a flavor and solvent for flavors.
safe_consumption: Acceptable Daily Intake is up to 6 mg/kg body weight with no known health effects when used in foods.

name: Triethyl citrate
description: An ester derived from citric acid used as an emulsifier in food products.
safe_consumption: Generally considered safe for consumption within recommended limits. Avoid excessive intake due to limited long-term studies on safety.

name: Ethanol
description: A basic component of alcoholic beverages and used as a solvent in various industries.
health_concerns: presence of toxic residues like methanol
safe_consumption: Consume ethanol-containing products responsibly. Avoid consumption by pregnant women or individuals with certain health conditions due to the presence of potentially harmful substances.

name: Glycerol monoacetate
description: A mixture of esters produced from the esterification of glycerol with acetic acid, used to enhance taste and aroma.
safe_consumption: Generally considered safe for consumption in small amounts as per existing descriptions. Further studies may be required for comprehensive safety assessment.

name: Glycerol diacetate
description: A synthetic additive manufactured chemically with glycerol and acetic acid.
safe_consumption: No known side effects to date, at dietary doses. However, the toxicology of diacetin would not be fully understood.

name: Triacetin
description: An artificial compound used in flavors, perfumes, and photographic development.
safe_consumption: Avoid if possible due to moderate concerns linked to studies; appears as an additive in some processed foods like snacks or beverages containing artificial flavors/smells.

name: Benzyl alcohol
description: A naturally occurring compound found in many plants, fruits and teas.
safe_consumption: Generally safe for consumption. Avoid if pregnant or breastfeeding due to potential risks associated with the 'panting' condition in infants.

name: Propylene glycol
description: Synthetic artificial industrial compound, produced in various ways.
health_concerns: serious damage to the nervous system
safe_consumption: May cause minor concerns for some people. Avoid large doses due to potential serious effects on nerves and other systems.

name: Polyethylene glycol
description: A synthetic polymer used as a carrier in food products, obtained by hydrolysis of Ethylene Oxide.
health_concerns: potentially less toxic due to long chain absorption
not completely absorbed by the intestine
safe_consumption: Generally considered safe for consumption. Long-term effects are not well understood and may vary among individuals.

name: Calcium lignosulfonate
description: A by-product of wood pulp production used as a carrier in food products.
safe_consumption: Daily intake up to 20 mg/kg body weight is considered safe for most individuals. No significant health concerns have been identified at this level of consumption.

name: Hydroxyethyl cellulose
description: A chemical compound derived from plant sources used as a thickener in food products.
safe_consumption: Generally recognized as safe for consumption by the general population. May cause minor allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.
